replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: ListAgents
tools.description: Lists agents you can SendMessage to — in-process subagents you spawned, the teammates on your team, other local Claude sessions on this machine, your Claude sessions running in the cloud (when this session has cloud access; a cloud session receives your message but cannot message any session back yet — do not ask it to reply, read its answer in its own transcript), and (when Remote Control is connected here) your account's other sessions — Remote Control sessions on other machines and cloud sessions, each row labeled by kind. Names are the address: send with `SendMessage({to: "<name>", message: "..."})`, copying the name exactly as a row prints it. Append a row's ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — two rows share it, or an error asks you to disambiguate.

channel.description: Not available in this build; leave unset.

q.description: Not available in this build; leave unset.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: DeferredToolPlaceholder
tools.description: Reserved placeholder that keeps deferred tool loading active; never call this tool.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

content.text:
<system-reminder>
Codebase and user instructions are shown below. Be sure to adhere to these instructions. IMPORTANT: These instructions OVERRIDE any default behavior and you MUST follow them exactly as written.

Contents of /home/runner/work/codeReader/codeReader/work/openinfer-project-openinfer/CLAUDE.md (project instructions, checked into the codebase):

This file provides guidance to Coding Agent when working with code in this repository.

## What is PegaInfer

Pure Rust + CUDA LLM inference engine. No PyTorch, no frameworks. OpenAI-compatible `/v1/completions` API.

**Supported models:**

Every model line is behind a cargo feature; only `qwen3` is a default feature, so the stock build is pure Rust + CUDA with no Python.

| Model | Crate | Feature flag | Architecture |
|-------|-------|-------------|-------------|
| Qwen3-4B / 8B | `pegainfer-qwen3` | `qwen3` (default) | Full attention, TP support |
| Qwen3.5-4B / 9B / 27B · Qwen3.8-27B | `pegainfer-qwen35` | `--features qwen35` (needs build-time Python + Triton) | Hybrid Gated DeltaNet + full attention. Qwen3.8 shares the line: same `model_type`, same text geometry — see `docs/models/qwen35/support-qwen38.md` |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite | `pegainfer-deepseek-v2-lite` | `--features deepseek-v2-lite` | MoE + EP, 2-GPU |
| Gemma 4 | `pegainfer-gemma4` | `--features gemma4` | Sliding-window + global full attention, dense sizes at TP2 (one rank per device), batched decode, opt-in chunked prefill (single rank only) |
| Kimi-K2 | `pegainfer-kimi-k2` | `--features kimi-k2` | MLA + MoE + Marlin INT4, 8-GPU EP |
| GLM5.2 | `pegainfer-glm52` | `--features glm52` | MLA + MoE + FP8, 8-GPU EP (bring-up) |
| Kimi-K3 | `pegainfer-k3` | `--features k3` | Hybrid KDA + MLA, latent MoE + MXFP4, EP (bring-up — single-rank decode wired) |

## Build & Run

**Always use `--release`** — debug builds are extremely slow for GPU/CUDA and will timeout.

When developing with Docker, use `docker/Dockerfile.dev` and `docker/dev.sh` as described in `docker/README.md`.

```bash
# Qwen3 (default feature, no Python anywhere in the build)
cargo run --release -- --model-path models/Qwen3-4B

# Feature-gated models
cargo run --release --features qwen35 -- --model-path models/Qwen3.5-4B
cargo run --release --features kimi-k2 -- --model-path models/Kimi-K2
cargo run --release --features deepseek-v2-lite -- --model-path models/DeepSeek-V2-Lite
cargo run --release --features glm52 -- --model-path models/GLM5.2
```

**Key env vars:**
- `PEGAINFER_CUDA_SM` — GPU SM target override when `nvidia-smi` unavailable (e.g. `120` or `120,80`)
- `PEGAINFER_TRITON_PYTHON` — Python with Triton for `qwen35` build-time AOT kernel generation (falls back to `.venv/bin/python`, then `python3`, then `python`)
- `PEGAINFER_TILELANG_PYTHON` — Python with TileLang for the `glm52` sparse-MLA build-time AOT (sm_90a targets only)
- `PEGAINFER_NCCL_ROOT` — NCCL root (>= 2.30.4) for DeepEP shim (`moe` feature)
- `PEGAINFER_FLASHINFER_INCLUDE` — FlashInfer include dir override
- `PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH` — override test model path (default: `models/Qwen3-4B`)
- `PEGAINFER_BUILD_TIMING=1` — print per-phase build timings (nvcc, Triton AOT, etc.)
- `PEGAINFER_NVCC_JOBS` — override parallel nvcc job count
- `PEGAINFER_GEMM_LT_CACHE` — opt-in cross-process cublasLt algo store: `<file>` carries the winners `gemm_lt_tune` timed in an earlier boot instead of re-timing them (Qwen3-4B on one sm_89 card: warm ready ~1965 → ~1312 ms, paired 5/5). Append-only text, created if absent, safe to share between processes and machines and safe to delete; each record carries GPU, CUDA runtime/driver/cublasLt version, shape and workspace cap, so anything that does not match is a miss and re-tunes (a driver update that keeps the same CUDA level is not distinguished — delete the file to force a re-tune). Unset = tune on every boot; Qwen3's `--batch-invariant` pins the heuristic instead and never reads it
- `PEGAINFER_GLOBAL_ATTN` — gemma4 global-attention kernel and pool format: unset/`off` = the incumbent kernel on the split K|V pool (byte-identical serving); `tilelang` = the generated kernel on the same pool; `tilelang640` = the generated kernel on a folded pool whose rows hold K only where the rotation touches it and fold K's norm weight into the query, 640 columns per token per head instead of 1024. Both generated states also read the sliding family's prompt rows through a generated windowed prefill and its pure-decode rows through a generated windowed split-KV kernel, project Q|K|V and gate|up with one GEMM each where the split state issues one per projection (the fused shape may round differently), need a build that carries the kernels, and report the global pool's bytes at start-up
- `PEGAINFER_KV_FP8` — gemma4 opt-in fp8 KV: `local` stores the sliding family's K/V as e4m3 at scale 1.0 (lossy; halves the local pool; refuses an enabled prefix cache; unset = byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_PREFIX_CACHE` — gemma4 opt-in conversation prefix cache: `K` entries of captured prompt state resume multi-turn prompts (pre-allocated page budget; unset = off, byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_ADMIT_COALESCE_MS` — gemma4 opt-in admission coalesce door: `N` ms in `1..=2000` (`off`/`0`/unset = admit on sight), holds arrivals that would invade a live decode batch so a window's arrivals land as one admission burst; refuses the async prefill lane; merging into one mixed step needs the chunked walk or a sub-budget prompt
- `PEGAINFER_ASYNC_PREFILL` — gemma4 opt-in overlap lane: `green:NN` prefills live-batch admissions on an SM-capped stream to protect decode tails (`shared` for comparison; unset = off; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` — gemma4 opt-in chunked walk: a mixed admission computes at most `N` prompt rows per step (`64 <= N <` the serving ceiling; unset = whole-prompt steps; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_GATHER_ROWS` / `PEGAINFER_MIX_MAX_PROMPTS` — gemma4 admission gather: how many prompt rows and how many prompts one mixed step may absorb (`1..=` the serving ceiling and `1..=` the decode slots; defaults gather only short bursts). Raising them lets a burst ride one step, which trades the median time to first token for the p99 tail and the wide-batch decode step; bad values refuse to start
- `PEGAINFER_MAX_CONTEXT` — gemma4 serving ceiling raise (default 8192, up to the checkpoint's 262144; a raise past the default needs `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` and refuses the async lane)
- `PEGAINFER_DECODE_SLOTS` — gemma4 decode slots (1..16, default 16): global KV budget = slots x ceiling, trade concurrency for context
- `GLM52_DECODE_SLOTS` / `GLM52_MTP_DRAFTS` — glm52 runtime profile: decode slots per rank (default 8, ceiling 32) and MTP draft span (default 5); `slots x (1+drafts)` must fit the 96-row step (validated at launch; MTP only). Throughput ceiling profile: `32` / `2`.
- `PEGAINFER_K3_CP` — k3 opt-in context-parallel prefill lane: CP width, must equal the process's local rank count (on a fleet each process runs its own gang; remote ranks pad). Mutually exclusive with the dspark draft lane.
- `PEGAINFER_K3_CP_MIN` — k3 CP admission floor in prompt tokens (default 2048; measured crossover ~1k). Prompts below it, or too long for one chunk step per rank (M0), prefill locally.

## Tests

```bash
# Unit tests (~9s)
cargo test --release --workspace --lib

# Lines gated on their own kernel feature need it named to run their unit tests.
# The K3 command also names the kernels crate, whose K3 tests ride the same
# feature:
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-k3 -p pegainfer-kernels --features k3 --lib
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-glm52 --features glm52 --lib

# Accuracy and integration tests — require GPU + model weights
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen3 --test hf_golden_gate
PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH=models/Qwen3.5-4B cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen35 --features qwen35 --test hf_golden_gate
PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH=models/Qwen3.5-4B cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen35 --features qwen35 --test e2e_scheduler

# Single test (filter by name)
cargo test --release --workspace --lib prefix_cache -- --nocapture
```

Qwen accuracy gates compare logits against stored HF golden fixtures. Qwen3.5 exact-text JSON baselines are retired; keep `e2e_scheduler` for scheduler liveness and request-flow coverage.

## Architecture

```
HTTP Request → vLLM frontend → EngineHandle → per-model scheduler/executor → TokenEvent
                                               │
              ┌──────────┬─────────────┬───────┼───────────┬──────────┐
              │          │             │       │           │          │
        pegainfer-  pegainfer-   pegainfer-  pegainfer-  pegainfer-  ...
        qwen3       qwen35       dsv2-lite   kimi-k2     glm52
      (full attn) (linear+full) (MoE+EP)   (MLA+MoE)  (MLA+MoE+FP8)
              │          │             │       │           │          │
              └──────────┴─────────────┴───────┼───────────┴──────────┘
                                               │
                          pegainfer-core runtime + pegainfer-kernels
                                               │
                               ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐
                               │               │               │
                       CUDA / cuBLAS    Triton AOT      FlashInfer
                                                    (sampling, attention,
                                                     norm, MLA decode)
```

**Key abstractions:**

- **`pegainfer-frontend`** — the serving frontend: the engine request/event contract (`pegainfer_frontend::engine` — `EngineHandle`, `GenerateRequest`, `TokenEvent`) plus the protocol stacks on top of it (`vllm` module today, `dynamo` planned) and the `ModelLine` dispatch trait. Model crates implement against the contract; the server binary does pure dispatch.
- **Per-model crates** — each model owns config, weights, prefill/decode execution, scheduler, tests, and benches.
- **`pegainfer-core::ops`** — shared GPU operator wrappers used by model crates.
- **`pegainfer-kernels`** — tensor/FFI/kernel build owner for CUDA, cuBLAS, FlashInfer, and Triton AOT. Model-specific kernels live in feature-gated submodules (`kimi_k2`, `glm52`).
- **CUDA Graph** — decode path captured inside model executors with pre-allocated buffers to preserve pointer stability.
- **KV state** — model schedulers own request state; shared paged-KV primitives live in `pegainfer-kv-cache`; host/SSD/RDMA offload bridge in `pegainfer-kv-offload`.

**Build system**: the virtual workspace root has no package build script. `pegainfer-kernels/build.rs` owns CUDA/Triton compilation:
1. Compiles `pegainfer-kernels/csrc/*.cu` with nvcc (auto-detects GPU SM targets)
2. Feature-gated codegen: `qwen35` runs Triton AOT via `pegainfer-kernels/tools/triton/gen_triton_aot.py`; `kimi-k2` adds MLA/MoE/Marlin CUDA; `glm52` adds MLA/MoE/FP8 CUDA plus TileLang sparse-MLA codegen on sm_90a

## EP Free-Running Discipline

Canonical doc: `docs/models/glm52/free-running-dp.md` (K3's gang lane follows it). Invariants — violating any of these is a deadlock design:

- **No rank ever stops or waits.** Every engine loop runs unconditionally at full speed; idle ranks step with padding rows. Any quiet wait (condvar, sleep-poll) inside EP coordination is a bug, and the fleet is never asleep, so never design "wake up" or "pump until X" steps.
- **The per-step collective chain is fixed** — no conditional collectives. Skipping work happens inside kernels via zero-load padding entry, never by host negotiation.
- **The launch count is the global clock** (pairing pins all ranks within ±1 launch). Coordination means agreeing ahead of time on *what step N contains*, never "wait until everyone is ready".
- **Padding rows are protocol surface**: their bytes reach peers, so every dummy-row input must be constructively deterministic.

# Team Documentation Workflow

Collaboration centered on the `docs/` directory.

## Knowledge Architecture (domain-axis)

Docs are organized by what they're *about*, not by lifecycle stage. A doc's freshness lives in its TL;DR (and `Last touched:` for active areas) — not by which directory it sits in. Completed work stays co-located with its domain. There is no `archives/` directory — if a doc no longer earns its keep, delete it; if a lasting lesson hides inside it, lift that lesson into `lessons/` first, then delete.

```
docs/
├── index.md           # Routing table — every doc must be listed here
├── roadmap/           # Strategic plans, quarterly direction, milestones
├── models/<line>/     # Per-model living docs (qwen3, qwen35, kimi-k2, ...)
│                      # — design, accuracy, perf, refactor records, gotchas
├── subsystems/<area>/ # Cross-cutting components (runtime, scheduler, frontend, kernels)
├── playbooks/         # Reusable how-to: benching, profiling, accuracy, onboarding
├── lessons/           # Tribal knowledge from research / other projects
├── benchmarks/        # Standalone benchmark snapshots and eval reports
├── conventions/       # Ongoing standards (bench regression, coding style)
└── private/           # Local-only notes (gitignored)
```

Classification rule at capture time:
- Is it tied to a specific model? → `models/<line>/`
- A specific subsystem? → `subsystems/<area>/`
- Reusable how-to applicable across models? → `playbooks/`
- Lasting lesson from elsewhere (other repo, research, postmortem)? → `lessons/`
- Snapshot of measurement, not a doc that evolves? → `benchmarks/`
- Strategic / cross-cutting plan? → `roadmap/`

If you can't pick one, the doc probably needs splitting.

## Documentation Style

- Docs cover what `--help` and code can't: pitfalls, diagnostic paths, decision context. Don't restate CLI reference.
- Every command in a doc must be run and verified before committing. Unverified commands are technical debt.
- The only required header is a one-line **TL;DR**. Keep it true; that's the contract.
- For `models/<line>/` and `subsystems/<area>/` docs, add `Last touched: YYYY-MM` and bump it when you do meaningful work on the doc (not for typo fixes). The date is a fact, not a judgement — readers infer freshness themselves.
- `playbooks/`, `lessons/`, `conventions/`, `roadmap/`, `benchmarks/`, `archives/` don't need a freshness stamp. They're either timeless until disproven, or self-dated, or explicitly inert.
- No `Status:` enum. Enum fields go stale exactly when you need them most.

## index.md Drift Policy

`index.md` is a routing table with a scanning-friendly TL;DR column. It is *allowed to drift* from the TL;DR inside each doc — the doc body is authoritative. Update `index.md` when you create or delete a doc, or when the existing TL;DR is so wrong it actively misleads. Don't churn it on every doc edit.

## Core Principles (CODE)

Documentation exists to advance work, not to hoard information. Four steps when handling information:

1. **Capture**: Only record what materially advances the project. When in doubt, leave it out.
2. **Organize**: Action-oriented. Resist the urge to organize for organization's sake — structure should be just enough.
3. **Distill**: Refactor over append. When you learn something new or hit a pitfall, integrate it into the document body — don't pile a changelog at the bottom.
4. **Express**: Every document must point to a next step. Split unwieldy documents proactively. Active documents must note the current blocker or next action.

## Collaboration Lifecycle

**Sync**

At the start of each session, you must read `index.md` and load the documents needed for the task at hand.

**Execute**
- Update relevant documents as you go. When a new problem or idea arises, create a document in the appropriate domain directory (see classification rule above).
- Record *why* a decision was made, not just *what* was done.

**Commit**

When a session wraps up:
- Update the TL;DR (and `Last touched`, where applicable) at the top of each modified document.
- Update `index.md` only when you created or deleted a doc, or when its TL;DR row is now misleading (see Drift Policy above).

## 前置讲义摘要（你必须基于这些已建立的认知继续，不要重复，要承接）

### u1-l1 从 PegaInfer 到 pegainfer-qwen35：crate 定位与混合架构总览

本讲建立 pegainfer-qwen35 的定位地图。PegaInfer 是纯 Rust + CUDA 推理引擎，请求经 frontend 契约（EngineHandle/TokenEvent）分派到各模型 crate。本 crate 是唯一混合架构线：全注意力层走分页 KV cache，Gated DeltaNet（GDN）线性注意力层以固定大小递推状态记忆历史，显存不随上下文增长（4B 为 8 full + 24 linear），故 crate 内并存 KV 与 recurrent 两套状态系统。Qwen3.8 因 model_type 与文本几何一致而共用此线。整个 crate 被 qwen35 feature 门控并转发至 kernels，构建期借 Python + Triton 生成 GDR chunkwise prefill 内核，默认构建保持无 Python。依赖边界：frontend 给契约、core 给共享算子、kernels 给专属内核、kv-cache 给分页 KV、sample 给采样。
### u1-l2 构建与运行：feature 门控与 Triton AOT 工具链

本讲拆解 pegainfer-qwen35 的构建体系：feature 门控、Triton AOT 工具链与测试入口。核心结论：qwen35 是跨 crate 联动开关——模型 crate 将 feature 转发给 kernels（空 feature，仅作编译期信号），驱动 build.rs 编译该线手写 CUDA 并执行 Triton AOT，模型代码与内核产物同进同退；feature 关闭时整个 crate 编译为空，默认构建不含 Python（CUDA 工具链仍必需）。AOT 链在构建期探测解释器、选定 SM 目标，为七个 GDR 分块预填充内核生成 cubin 与 C 包装，修补多设备句柄后编成静态库，经三级 FFI 重导出由 recurrent.rs 启动。集成测试与基准以 required-features 门控；model_fixture 夹具依模型路径环境变量校验权重，无效即 SKIP 安静通过。关键术语：feature 转发、空 feature、build.rs、AOT/JIT、SM 架构代号、required-features。
### u1-l3 目录结构与模块地图：src/ 各文件职责速览

本讲绘制 pegainfer-qwen35 的模块地图：src/ 共 31 个文件约 1.6 万行，按职责归为配置、权重、执行、调度、缓存、TP 六大类；TP、执行、调度各占约四分之一，配置最小却是所有路径必经之地。核心结论：lib.rs 的 mod 声明即 crate 目录页，可见性修饰本身就是 API 边界；公开面分三层——正门（model_line、start_engine*）给根服务器，runtime 与 runtime_ops 两个侧门仅供本 crate 测试、调试与基准。双路径分叉仅两处：启动函数按设备数分叉（单 GPU 先载权重再起调度器，TP 整体委托）与 SchedulerBackend 枚举；TP 专属模块仅 4 个，单 GPU 专属仅 unified_forward，其余皆为共享底座。关键术语：六大类、三层公开面、双路径分叉、控制器-worker 结构、三来源算子面（core 通用、kernels 专属、本 crate 封装）。后续单元按 config→weights→执行→scheduler→prefix_cache→tp_executor 顺序逐一放大此地图。
### u1-l4 ModelLine 接入：probe、CLI 增补与服务计划

本讲主线 src/model_line.rs：Qwen35Line 实现 ModelLine trait，服务器只做纯分派、不认识模型类型。probe 两段式认领身份（外层「或」、内层「与」），认身份不认版本，Qwen3.8 因此共用此线。旗标分核心/共享/专属三层，遵循「消费或拒绝」纪律，不归属即报错。validate 为六条有序规则链、首错即返：stream 重叠批次上限 32 源于 cuBLAS 多流风险，TP 下拒重叠与 auto 策略。serve_plan 把 auto 工具解析器定为 qwen3_coder，修复按路径子串误判的线上 bug，显式指定仍优先；同批规则在库边界纵深再校验。
### u2-l1 config.json 的解析与校验：从 RawConfig 到 Config35

本讲剖析 pegainfer-qwen35 的配置加载链：config.json 先由 serde 反序列化为忠实镜像磁盘结构的 RawConfig/TextConfig（只查形状），再经 `TryFrom` 唯一边界一次性校验为 Config35（查语义），错误收入类型化枚举 ConfigError（14 个变体），十步有序检查首错即返，贯彻 fail-closed 与「不可表示非法状态」原则；from_file 收尾还按优先级解析 eos_token_ids。关键概念：layer_types 字符串在此升格为 LayerType（full/linear_attention 二值），表达混合架构的层排布；内核 AOT 烘焙维度门（GDN head dim 128、全注意力 256、卷积核宽 1..=4）在加载期对拍；rotary_dim 由 head_dim 乘 partial_rotary_factor 截断而得（部分旋转）。三个词表宽度各司其职：vocab_size 为嵌入物理行数，decodable_vocab 为稠密可解码前缀（tokenizer 过宽或 id 有洞即拒载），selection_vocab 经 bound_selection_vocab 在权重加载前 128 对齐并夹紧、供 cublasLt 快路径，padding 行采样前压 -inf。Config35 刻意对张量并行无知，TP 几何留给下一讲的 LocalGeometry。
### u2-l2 张量并行几何：TensorParallelConfig 与 LocalGeometry

### u2-l4 层结构：TransformerBlock35 与两种注意力层

本讲精读 qwen35 的层结构。核心模块是 TransformerBlock35：持有两种层共有的 input/post_attention 双 norm 与 MLP35，注意力子层封装为枚举 LayerKind（FullAttentionLayer / LinearAttentionLayer）；config.layer_types 在加载期决定装配成哪个变体（checkpoint 前缀分别为 self_attn / linear_attn），前向期 match 分派。贯穿性结论：层结构体只装不可变权重——全注意力的 K/V 写入模型级共享分页池（仅按全注意力层数开池，用 full_idx 索引），线性注意力（Gated DeltaNet）的递推状态与卷积状态外置于调度器侧的 RecurrentState（用 linear_idx 索引），这一权重与状态分离是 CUDA Graph 指针稳定和前缀缓存的前提。全注意力层引入 gated Q（q_proj 行含 per-head [q|gate] 交错块，TP 须按 head 整块切）、head 共享 QK-norm、partial RoPE 及「norm+RoPE+落页」融合预备内核。线性注意力层引入装载期 vstack 融合（in_proj_qkvz / in_proj_ba）、因果 depthwise conv1d、GDR chunkwise 递推与 z 门控 RMSNorm。所有 norm 为 (1+w) 变体；TP 通信点统一在回到 hidden 维处（o_proj / out_proj 后 all_reduce_hidden），prefill 与 decode 前向五步同构。

本讲以 Qwen3.5-4B 为例精读全注意力层 hd256 内核族的 prefill/decode 调用链。核心结论：partial RoPE 缓存加载期一次建满（rotary_dim=64，half-split 重复布局，frequency_dim 取 rotary_dim 以对齐 checkpoint），运行期守卫 ensure_rope_cache_covers 只校验、不扩容；分页 KV 池按「页→层→K/V 块→token→head→dim」嵌套，由 KvLayout 三个步长描述，请求个体性全部收敛在 KvView 页表；prefill 由 PrefillPagedPlan 携带页表元数据，融合预备内核一次完成 qk_norm、partial RoPE 与 K/V 落页，decode 预备内核不碰池、落页藏在注意力包装开头的 scatter，位置从标量 start_pos 变为每请求 positions_d；hd256 是编译期门（head_dim≠256 拒载），sm_scale=1/√256 取全头维；decode 按 GQA 组比率三路由——比率不在编译清单走 via_prefill 回退（仅 Serve），bs≤16 且比率恰为 4 走 split-KV（splits 按桶固定以稳定 CUDA Graph 网格），否则 FlashInfer 批量内核；TP 不改变组比率。

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

# 线性注意力层：Gated DeltaNet 的状态与更新

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 写出 `per_layer_dims` 的两条元素数公式，并对任一配置手算一层线性注意力的 state 与 conv_state 元素数、字节数。
2. 解释 `RecurrentState` / `LayerRecurrentState` 的 `[H,K,V]` f32 状态与 bf16 conv_state 布局，以及两种精度各自的选择理由。
3. 说明 causal conv1d 在 prefill 与 decode 两条路径上如何读写状态。
4. 解释 `LinearStatePointerTables` 为什么能让「批量内核 + CUDA Graph」同时成立。
5. 推导 TP 下 recurrent/conv 状态按 value head 分片、从不 all-reduce 的不变量，并证明分片后各 rank 状态之和恰好等于 TP1 总量。

## 2. 前置知识

**线性注意力与全注意力的记忆方式对比。** 全注意力层把历史上每个 token 的 K/V 都存进分页 KV 池，注意力计算时 \(Q K^\top V\) 要回看全部历史，显存随上下文长度线性增长。Gated DeltaNet（GDN，Qwen3.5 线性注意力层的底层模型）换了一种「记忆」：每个头维护一个**固定大小**的递推状态矩阵 \(S \in \mathbb{R}^{d_k \times d_v}\)，每来一个 token 就对状态做一次**门控衰减 + delta（误差校正）写入**，输出由查询直接读状态得到。历史信息被「压缩」进这个矩阵里，因此显存不随上下文增长——这正是 u1-l1 说的「4B 为 8 full + 24 linear」中 24 个 linear 层的记忆载体。

**两个短术语：**

- **FLA `[H,K,V]` 约定**：状态张量按「头 → key 维 → value 维」嵌套存放，value 维连续。本 crate 的状态是「每头一个 \([d_k, d_v]\) 矩阵，头之间依次拼接」的一维 f32 数组。
- **depthwise conv1d（因果卷积）**：每个通道独立做一维卷积，只看当前和过去 \(k_{conv}-1\) 个输入。GDN 用它给 qkv 做一层短程平滑，需要保存最近的卷积抽头（taps）。

**承接 u2-l4 的关键结论**：层结构体（`LinearAttentionLayer`）只装**不可变权重**；递推状态**外置**在调度器侧的 `RecurrentState` 里。本讲就放大这个「外置的状态」：它的布局公式、它如何被内核原地更新、以及批量执行时如何被指针表索引。权重侧的装载期融合（`in_proj_qkvz`、`in_proj_ba`）与 z 门控 RMSNorm 已在 u2-l4 讲过，本讲只在使用点引用。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 状态布局：per_layer_dims 与 [H,K,V] f32 状态 + bf16 conv_state

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

`RecurrentState` 是**一个请求**在某一时刻的全部线性注意力状态：24 个线性层（以 4B 为例）各持一份 `LayerRecurrentState`，外加一个 host 侧的 `seq_len` 计数器。每个 `LayerRecurrentState` 有两块设备内存：

- **state**：GDN 递推状态，\([H_v^{local} \times d_k \times d_v]\) 个 **f32**。这是「被压缩的历史」，随每个 token 做门控衰减与 delta 写入，是长期累积量。
- **conv_state**：因果卷积抽头，\([d_{qkv}^{local} \times (k_{conv}-1)]\) 个 **bf16**。它只是「最近 \(k_{conv}-1\) 个输入的原样字节」，不参与任何算术累积。

「状态外置于层结构体」是三个后续机制的前提：CUDA Graph 指针稳定（u4-l3）、前缀缓存快照（u6）、prefill/decode 状态交接（u4-l1）。本讲先把布局本身讲透。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

一层线性注意力的两个状态尺寸由同一个小函数决定：

\[
S_{state} = H_v^{local} \times d_k \times d_v \quad (\text{f32 元素})
\]

\[
S_{conv} = d_{qkv}^{local} \times (k_{conv} - 1) \quad (\text{bf16 元素})
\]

其中融合 qkv 投影的本地宽度（q 段与 k 段等宽，v 段按 value head 计）：

\[
d_{qkv}^{local} = 2 \times (H_k^{local} \times d_k) + H_v^{local} \times d_v
\]

一个请求的总状态字节：

\[
B_{req} = L_{linear} \times (S_{state} \times 4 + S_{conv} \times 2)
\]

伪代码（分配路径）：

```text
RecurrentState::new(ctx, config, geometry):
    (L, S_state, S_conv) = per_layer_dims(config, geometry)
    for _ in 0..L:                      # 每个线性层一份
        state      = alloc_zeros::<f32>(S_state)     # 零初始化：空历史
        conv_state = DeviceVec::zeros(S_conv)        # 零抽头
    seq_len = 0
```

#### 4.1.4 代码实践

**实践目标**：用 `per_layer_dims` 公式手算 Qwen3.5-4B（TP1）一层线性注意力的 state/conv 元素数与字节数，再核算 64 个 decode 槽（含 prefill 瞬态，×2）的总显存预留，并与源码内嵌单测对拍。

**操作步骤**（纸面计算，4B 配置：`num_hidden_layers=32`、8 full + 24 linear，`linear_num_key_heads=16`、`linear_num_value_heads=32`、`linear_key_head_dim=linear_value_head_dim=128`、`linear_conv_kernel_dim=4`，TP1 故 local 即 global）：

1. state 元素数：\(32 \times 128 \times 128 = 524{,}288\) 个 f32 → 每层 2 MiB。
2. \(d_{qkv} = 2\times(16\times128) + 32\times128 = 8192\)；conv 元素数：\(8192 \times (4-1) = 24{,}576\) 个 bf16 → 每层 48 KiB。
3. 每层字节 \(= 524288\times4 + 24576\times2 = 2{,}146{,}304\)；每请求 \( \times 24\) 层 \(= 51{,}511{,}296\) B \(= 49.125\) MiB（即 49 MiB + 128 KiB）。
4. 64 槽预留：\(2 \times 64 \times 49.125\text{ MiB} = 6288\text{ MiB} \approx 6.14\text{ GiB}\)。
5. 与 [src/recurrent_state.rs:L243-L252](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/recurrent_state.rs#L243-L252) 的内嵌单测 `qwen35_4b_recurrent_allocation_is_49_125_mib` 对拍——它用同样的常数断言 `bytes == 49*1024*1024 + 128*1024`。这是纯 host 算术测试，不需要 GPU 设备，但编译需要 CUDA + Triton AOT 工具链（见 u1-l2）。

**需要观察的现象**：若本地有构建工具链，运行 `cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen35 --features qwen35 --lib recurrent` 应通过；启动真实服务时，[src/weights.rs:L322-L326](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/weights.rs#L322-L326) 的 info 日志会打出 `recurrent-state reserve: ... MB (2 x 64 slots)`，应与你手算的 6288 MiB 一致。

**预期结果**：每请求 49.125 MiB；64 槽 × 2 ≈ 6.14 GiB。若在无工具链环境，纸面结果即最终产出，运行验证标注「待本地验证」。

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：对 [src/config/model.rs:L303-L324](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/config/model.rs#L303-L324) 测试夹具 `VALID_RAW`（`linear_num_key_heads=16`、`linear_num_value_heads=48`、head dim 均 128、卷积宽 4、1 个线性层）计算 TP1 下的 state/conv 元素数。
**答案**：state \(= 48\times128\times128 = 786{,}432\) 个 f32（3 MiB）；\(d_{qkv} = 2\times(16\times128)+48\times128 = 10240\)，conv \(= 10240\times3 = 30{,}720\) 个 bf16（60 KiB）。

**练习 2**：为什么 state 用 f32 而 conv_state 用 bf16？
**答案**：state 是跨整个序列持续累积的递推量，每步都在旧值上做衰减与更新，量化误差会随序列长度复利放大，所以按上游 `mamba_ssm_dtype="float32"` 约定用 f32，且两个 GDN 内核封装的指针也确实按 `*mut f32` 传递。conv_state 只是把最近 \(k_{conv}-1\) 个 **bf16 输入原样**留存，不参与累积，用 bf16 存是无损的，还省一半显存。

**练习 3**：把 `linear_conv_kernel_dim` 改成 5 会发生什么？
**答案**：加载即失败，返回 `ConfigError::LinearConvKernelDim { max: 4, actual: 5 }`——因为 in-tree 的 `conv1d.cu` 只为 `kernel_size - 1 <= 3` 个抽头携带状态（`LINEAR_CONV_MAX_KERNEL_DIM`，见 [src/config/model.rs:L248-L253](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/config/model.rs#L248-L253)）。

### 4.2 causal conv1d：短记忆的入口与 prefill/decode 两条内核

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

在进入 GDN 递推之前，线性层先把融合投影出的 qkv 段过一遍**因果 depthwise conv1d**（再接 SiLU）。它是「短记忆」：只看最近 \(k_{conv}\) 个输入（当前 + 状态里的 \(k_{conv}-1\) 个抽头），输出写回给 GDN。卷积状态就是那 \(k_{conv}-1\) 个抽头，oldest-first 排列。

同一个语义有两套内核：

- **prefill**：一次处理整段（一个 chunk 的）token 序列，内核内部能直接看到历史 token，只需在结束时把**最后 \(k_{conv}-1\) 个输入**写进 conv_state，供下一段接续。
- **decode**：每个请求只有 1 个新 token，历史只能来自 conv_state；内核读抽头、算输出、**原地滚动**抽头，并与 SiLU 融合（输出是 `silu(bf16(conv))`，不是 `silu(sum)`， rounding 与参考实现逐位一致）。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

decode 一步（对槽 \(i\)、通道 \(c\)，卷积宽 \(k\)，抽头宽 \(w = k-1\)）：

\[
out_c = \mathrm{silu}\big(\mathrm{bf16}(\textstyle\sum_{j=0}^{k-1} w_{c,j} \cdot tap_{c,j})\big), \quad tap = [\,\underbrace{state_c[0..w]}_{\text{旧抽头}},\, x_c\,]
\]

随后状态滚动（oldest-first 移位，新输入顶到末位）：

\[
state_c[j] \leftarrow state_c[j+1]\ (j<w-1), \qquad state_c[w-1] \leftarrow x_c
\]

这正是 [src/recurrent.rs:L616-L647](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/recurrent.rs#L616-L647) 里参考实现 `reference_conv1d_decode_step` 逐行写成的内容——测试用它给 GPU 内核对拍。

#### 4.2.3 源码精读

- [src/recurrent.rs:L54-L87](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/recurrent.rs#L54-L87) — `conv1d_prefill_batch_into`：对整段 `x_seq` 做因果卷积并更新 `conv_state`。开头的四个断言就是状态契约：`conv_weight.len == num_channels * kernel_size`、`conv_state.len == num_channels * (kernel_size - 1)`，且输入输出同形。
- [../pegainfer-kernels/src/ops/qwen35.rs:L599-L650](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-kernels/src/ops/qwen35.rs#L599-L650) — `conv1d_decode_batch_into`：批量 decode 版。签名里没有「每个槽的状态」数组本体，只有 `conv_state_ptrs: &CudaSlice<u64>`——设备侧指针数组，第 \(i\) 行指向槽 \(i\) 的 conv_state，内核**原地更新**。文档还约定：输入 `x` 可以是融合 qkvz 投影的 qkv 波段（槽按张量自身行宽跨步），`kernel_size` 不得超过 4。

### 4.3 LinearStatePointerTables：为批量内核准备的每槽指针表

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

批解码一步要同时更新 N 个请求 × 24 个线性层的状态。若每个请求单独持有 `RecurrentState`，内核无法用一次发射索引到它们——CUDA 内核需要**设备侧连续的指针数组**。`LinearStatePointerTables` 就是这张表：每个线性层 ℓ 配一对 `CudaSlice<u64>`（`state_ptrs[ℓ]`、`conv_state_ptrs[ℓ]`），第 \(i\) 行是槽 \(i\) 的该层状态设备地址。

它成立的前提是一个不变量：**槽 \(i\) 的状态分配在请求生命周期内地址永不改变**。于是表可以一次建好、每个 decode token 反复重放——这正是 CUDA Graph 捕获需要的指针稳定性（图里烤进了这些地址，重放时读写同一位置）。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

一次批解码中线性层的执行序列（`padded_bs` 行，含 padding）：

```text
batch_decode_linear_attention_slots(attn, state_ptrs[ℓ], conv_state_ptrs[ℓ], padded_bs):
1. qkvz = GEMM(in_proj_qkvz, normed)          # [qkv+z, padded_bs]
2. ba   = GEMM(in_proj_ba,   normed)          # [2*Hv, padded_bs]
3. qkv_conv = conv1d_decode_batch(qkvz[:, :qkv_dim], conv_w, conv_state_ptrs[ℓ])
                                            # 内核按指针表原地滚动各槽 conv_state
4. o = gdr_decode_batch(qkv_conv, ba[:, :Hv], ba[:, Hv:], dt_bias, a_log, state_ptrs[ℓ])
                                            # 内核按指针表原地更新各槽 GDN state
5. g = rms_norm_gated(o, norm_w, z=qkvz[:, qkv_dim:])
6. attn_results = GEMM(out_proj, g); all_reduce_hidden(attn_results)   # TP 唯一通信点
```

表的两种构建方式：

- **固定行集**（单 GPU 图解码）：`from_recurrent_refs` 按精确 batch 建表填满，一次成型。
- **行集每步变化**（eager TP 解码）：`with_capacity` 按容量建一次空表，每步 `refill_from_recurrent_refs` 只把**活跃行** H2D 覆写进既有分配——零每步分配。

### 4.4 TP 分片不变量：按 value head 分片、从不 all-reduce

#### 4.4.1 概念说明

GDN 状态天然按 value head 可分：状态是「每头一个 \([d_k, d_v]\) 矩阵」，头与头之间在递推中**互不交换数据**。于是 TP 的切法是：把 \(H_v\) 个 value head（连同 qkv 投影的对应行段、beta/alpha/dt_bias/a_log 等每头向量）均匀分给各 rank，每个 rank 只为自己那 \(H_v/W\) 个头维护并更新状态。分片是不相交的——各 rank 状态拼起来恰是完整状态，因此**没有任何理由对状态做 all-reduce**。

跨 rank 聚合只发生在回到 hidden 维的那一刻：`out_proj` 是行并行（各 rank 算出 hidden 维的**部分和**），随后一次 `all_reduce_hidden` 求和。这与 u2-l4 的结论「TP 通信点统一在回到 hidden 维处」一致，且模块文档直接写明状态「never all-reduced」。

#### 4.4.2 核心流程

TP 下每 rank 的状态尺寸：

\[
H_v^{local} = H_v / W, \qquad H_k^{local} = H_k / W
\]

\[
S_{state}^{local} = \frac{H_v}{W} \times d_k \times d_v, \qquad
S_{conv}^{local} = \Big(2 \frac{H_k}{W} d_k + \frac{H_v}{W} d_v\Big)(k_{conv}-1)
\]

分片正确性依赖两条上游约束：

1. **头分组不变量**（Config35 层）：\(H_v\) 是 \(H_k\) 的整数倍（一个 key head 服务一组 value head），`ConfigError::LinearHeadDivisibility` 强制。
2. **整除门**（LocalGeometry 层）：\(H_k\)（连同注意力头、KV 头、intermediate）必须被 \(W\) 整除，`TpIndivisible` fail-closed。

由 1、2 可推出 \(H_v\) 免检：设 \(H_v = m \cdot H_k\) 且 \(H_k = W \cdot k\)，则 \(H_v = W \cdot (m k)\)，自动整除——这就是 tp.rs 文档说「value-head count follows from the Config35 key/value-head invariant」的推理链。

每个 rank 状态字节占总量的比例：

\[
\frac{B_{req}^{local}}{B_{req}} = \frac{1}{W}
\]

（qkv 通道同样按行分片，conv 状态也随之精确减半。）**精确 \(1/W\)、零复制、零通信**。

#### 4.4.4 代码实践

**实践目标**：用数字验证「TP 下各 rank 状态精确减半、总和不变」，体会免检推理。

**操作步骤**（4B 配置，TP2）：

1. \(H_v^{local} = 32/2 = 16\)，\(H_k^{local} = 16/2 = 8\)。
2. state：\(16 \times 128 \times 128 = 262{,}144\) f32 = 1 MiB/层。
3. \(d_{qkv}^{local} = 2\times(8\times128) + 16\times128 = 4096\)；conv：\(4096\times3 = 12{,}288\) bf16 = 24 KiB/层。
4. 每请求每 rank：\(24 \times (1\,\text{MiB} + 24\,\text{KiB}) = 25{,}755{,}648\) B = 24.5625 MiB；两 rank 合计 \(= 49.125\) MiB，与 TP1 每请求总量**逐字节相等**。
5. 复核免检链：\(H_v = 32 = 2 \times H_k = 2 \times 16\)，\(H_k = 2 \times 8\) ⟹ \(H_v = 2 \times (2\times 8)\)，被 2 整除。再用 [src/config/tp.rs:L342-L359](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/config/tp.rs#L342-L359) 的测试 `requires_linear_attention_key_head_divisibility` 确认：只有 key head 不整除时才报 `TpIndivisible`。

**需要观察的现象**：第 4 步的两 rank 合计与 4.1.4 手算的 TP1 每请求字节数完全相同（51,511,296 B）——分片零复制、零冗余。

**预期结果**：TP2 每 rank 24.5625 MiB/请求；64 槽 × 2 预留在每 rank 上约 \(128 \times 24.5625 = 3144\) MiB ≈ 3.07 GiB（TP 每卡只需一半状态显存）。纸面可完成，无需设备。

#### 4.4.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：为什么 GDN 状态从不 all-reduce，而 MLP 的输出要 all-reduce？
**答案**：状态按 value head 不相交分片，各 rank 更新的切片拼起来就是完整状态，无信息重叠；而 `down_proj`/`out_proj` 是行并行，各 rank 只产出 hidden 维部分和，必须求和才能得到正确残差流。通信只发生在「回到 hidden 维」处。

**练习 2**：如果某配置 \(H_k = 17\)、\(H_v = 34\)、W=2，会触发哪个错误？
**答案**：`ConfigError::TpIndivisible { field: "linear_num_key_heads", value: 17, world_size: 2 }`。注意 \(H_v = 34\) 虽然能被 2 整除也救不了——免检的前提是 \(H_k\) 先过整除门，这正是 tp.rs 测试刻意保持 value = 2×key 不变量再只打破 key 整除性的原因。

**练习 3**：TP 下 f32 状态的精度策略变了吗？
**答案**：没有。状态仍是每 rank 本地的 f32 `[H,K,V]`，公式与内核与 TP1 完全相同（TP1 契约：W=1 时 local 即 global）；TP 改变的只是头数，而头数是内核的运行期参数。

## 5. 综合实践

为 Qwen3.5-4B 建立一份「**GDN 状态账本**」，把本讲全部内容串起来：

1. **布局列**（4.1）：对 TP1 与 TP2 各列一行——每层 state 元素数/字节、conv 元素数/字节、每请求 24 层总字节。来源：`per_layer_dims` 与 `bytes_per_request` 手算。
2. **预留列**（4.1）：`STATES_PER_DECODE_SLOT=2 × 64 槽`的 recurrent 预留（TP1 ≈ 6.14 GiB，TP2 每 rank ≈ 3.07 GiB），并注明它在 weights.rs 显存预算顺序中的位置（scratch → recurrent → snapshot → KV 池余量 85%）。
3. **实例清单**（4.1/4.3）：用 Grep 找出所有 `RecurrentState::new` 调用点并注明角色——图槽 ×64（`batch_decode_graph.rs`）、prefill 瞬态（`scheduler/backend.rs::alloc_recurrent`、`unified_forward.rs`）、teacher-force 执行器（`executor.rs`）、前缀快照槽（`prefix_cache.rs::RecurrentStateStore`）。每份的大小都由同一个 `bytes_per_request` 决定。
4. **寻址链**（4.3）：画「槽 → 指针表 → 内核」的箭头图，标注 `copy_state_to_slot` / `move_slot_within` 两个原语作用在哪条边上，并写一句为什么两者都不改地址。
5. **验证**（有构建工具链时）：跑 `cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen35 --features qwen35 --lib recurrent`，确认 `qwen35_4b_recurrent_allocation_is_49_125_mib` 与你的账本一致；无工具链则账本本身就是交付物，运行验证标注「待本地验证」。

完成标准：账本中任何一个数字都能回溯到 `per_layer_dims` / `bytes_per_request` 的一次代入，且 TP1 与 TP×W 的数字满足「每 rank = 总量 / W」。

## 6. 本讲小结

- `RecurrentState` = 24 份 `LayerRecurrentState` + `seq_len`；每层是 `[H_v^local·d_k·d_v]` 个 f32（GDN 递推状态，长期累积故用 f32）+ `[d_qkv^local·(k_conv-1)]` 个 bf16（卷积抽头，原样字节故用 bf16）。
- 所有尺寸出自唯一的 `per_layer_dims`；分配、显存预留、前缀快照槽数共享它，4B 每请求 49.125 MiB。
- causal conv1d 有 prefill（整段 + 末尾抽头落盘）与 decode（读抽头、原地滚动、融合 SiLU）两套内核，`conv1d_prefill_handoff` 证明 chunk 接力与整段等价。
- `LinearStatePointerTables` 用「槽地址终身不变」换来一次建表、token 间重放，是批量内核与 CUDA Graph 同时成立的前提；状态迁移原语一律向既有分配写入。
- TP 按 value head（连同 qkv 通道与每头向量）不相交分片，状态从不 all-reduce；唯一通信点是 `out_proj` 后的 `all_reduce_hidden`，各 rank 状态精确等于总量的 1/W。
- 头数是运行期参数、head dim 是编译期烘焙（128/128、卷积宽 ≤4）——config 加载期的三条门就是这两层事实的守门人。

## 7. 下一步学习建议

- **u3-l3（FFI 边界与内核封装）**：本讲只把 `gated_delta_rule_prefill_chunkwise_into` 当黑盒流水线；下一讲拆 `unsafe` FFI 调用的指针 guard 生命周期、`device_ptr`/`device_ptr_mut` 模式与 chunkwise 七段的算子契约。
- **u4-l1（Prefill 分块）**：本讲看到 conv/GDR 状态在单 chunk 内推进；下一讲看 `PREFILL_CHUNK_LEN` 如何把长提示切成 chunk 串行接力，以及 `GdrChunkwiseScratch35` 的保守预留。
- **u6-l1/l2（前缀缓存）**：`RecurrentStateStore` 的快照槽就是本讲的 `RecurrentState` 按预算复用——建议带着「快照 = 状态字节照搬」的直觉去读 `PrefixBoundaryKey` 与恢复路径。
- 想先摸执行全景的读者也可跳到 **u4-l2（batch_decode）**：本讲 4.3.2 的六步序列就是它核心循环的线性层分支。

# 线性注意力层：Gated DeltaNet 的状态与更新

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 写出 `per_layer_dims` 的两条元素数公式，并对任一配置手算一层线性注意力的 state 与 conv_state 元素数、字节数。
2. 解释 `RecurrentState` / `LayerRecurrentState` 的 `[H,K,V]` f32 状态与 bf16 conv_state 布局，以及两种精度各自的选择理由。
3. 说明 causal conv1d 在 prefill 与 decode 两条路径上如何读写状态。
4. 解释 `LinearStatePointerTables` 为什么能让「批量内核 + CUDA Graph」同时成立。
5. 推导 TP 下 recurrent/conv 状态按 value head 分片、从不 all-reduce 的不变量，并证明分片后各 rank 状态之和恰好等于 TP1 总量。

## 2. 前置知识

**线性注意力与全注意力的记忆方式对比。** 全注意力层把历史上每个 token 的 K/V 都存进分页 KV 池，注意力计算时 \(Q K^\top V\) 要回看全部历史，显存随上下文长度线性增长。Gated DeltaNet（GDN，Qwen3.5 线性注意力层的底层模型）换了一种「记忆」：每个头维护一个**固定大小**的递推状态矩阵 \(S \in \mathbb{R}^{d_k \times d_v}\)，每来一个 token 就对状态做一次**门控衰减 + delta（误差校正）写入**，输出由查询直接读状态得到。历史信息被「压缩」进这个矩阵里，因此显存不随上下文增长——这正是 u1-l1 说的「4B 为 8 full + 24 linear」中 24 个 linear 层的记忆载体。

**两个短术语：**

- **FLA `[H,K,V]` 约定**：状态张量按「头 → key 维 → value 维」嵌套存放，value 维连续。本 crate 的状态是「每头一个 \([d_k, d_v]\) 矩阵，头之间依次拼接」的一维 f32 数组。
- **depthwise conv1d（因果卷积）**：每个通道独立做一维卷积，只看当前和过去 \(k_{conv}-1\) 个输入。GDN 用它给 qkv 做一层短程平滑，需要保存最近的卷积抽头（taps）。

**承接 u2-l4 的关键结论**：层结构体（`LinearAttentionLayer`）只装**不可变权重**；递推状态**外置**在调度器侧的 `RecurrentState` 里。本讲就放大这个「外置的状态」：它的布局公式、它如何被内核原地更新、以及批量执行时如何被指针表索引。权重侧的装载期融合（`in_proj_qkvz`、`in_proj_ba`）与 z 门控 RMSNorm 已在 u2-l4 讲过，本讲只在使用点引用。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

| 文件 | 行数 | 作用 |
|------|------|------|
| `src/recurrent_state.rs` | 252 | 本讲主角：状态布局公式、`RecurrentState` 分配/拷贝、`LinearStatePointerTables` 指针表、每请求字节数 |
| `src/config/model.rs` | 433 | `Config35` 中线性注意力几何字段与内核维度门（GDN 128/128、卷积宽 1..=4） |
| `src/config/tp.rs` | 360 | `LocalGeometry` 的 `local_linear_*` 派生与 TP 整除门 |
| `src/recurrent.rs` | 1360 | 内核封装：conv1d prefill、GDR 单槽 decode（测试用）、GDR chunkwise prefill 七段流水线 |
| `src/batch_decode.rs` | ~950 | 批解码主循环：`batch_decode_linear_attention_slots` 一次线性层解码的完整算子序列 |
| `src/batch_decode_graph.rs` | 169 | `slot_states` 槽位与指针表的建表、`copy_state_to_slot` / `move_slot_within` |
| `src/prefill.rs` | ~560 | prefill 侧线性层前向：状态在 chunk 间的推进 |
| `src/weights.rs` | ~700 | `STATES_PER_DECODE_SLOT=2` 预留、显存预算顺序、`all_reduce_hidden` |
| `src/weights/layers.rs` | 300+ | `LinearAttentionLayer` 权重定义（本讲只引用维度注释） |
| `../pegainfer-kernels/src/ops/qwen35.rs` | 650+ | 批量 decode 内核的 Rust 封装与文档契约（`state_ptrs: &CudaSlice<u64>`） |

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 状态布局：per_layer_dims 与 [H,K,V] f32 状态 + bf16 conv_state

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

`RecurrentState` 是**一个请求**在某一时刻的全部线性注意力状态：24 个线性层（以 4B 为例）各持一份 `LayerRecurrentState`，外加一个 host 侧的 `seq_len` 计数器。每个 `LayerRecurrentState` 有两块设备内存：

- **state**：GDN 递推状态，\([H_v^{local} \times d_k \times d_v]\) 个 **f32**。这是「被压缩的历史」，随每个 token 做门控衰减与 delta 写入，是长期累积量。
- **conv_state**：因果卷积抽头，\([d_{qkv}^{local} \times (k_{conv}-1)]\) 个 **bf16**。它只是「最近 \(k_{conv}-1\) 个输入的原样字节」，不参与任何算术累积。

「状态外置于层结构体」是三个后续机制的前提：CUDA Graph 指针稳定（u4-l3）、前缀缓存快照（u6）、prefill/decode 状态交接（u4-l1）。本讲先把布局本身讲透。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

一层线性注意力的两个状态尺寸由同一个小函数决定：

\[
S_{state} = H_v^{local} \times d_k \times d_v \quad (\text{f32 元素})
\]

\[
S_{conv} = d_{qkv}^{local} \times (k_{conv} - 1) \quad (\text{bf16 元素})
\]

其中融合 qkv 投影的本地宽度（q 段与 k 段等宽，v 段按 value head 计）：

\[
d_{qkv}^{local} = 2 \times (H_k^{local} \times d_k) + H_v^{local} \times d_v
\]

一个请求的总状态字节：

\[
B_{req} = L_{linear} \times (S_{state} \times 4 + S_{conv} \times 2)
\]

伪代码（分配路径）：

```text
RecurrentState::new(ctx, config, geometry):
    (L, S_state, S_conv) = per_layer_dims(config, geometry)
    for _ in 0..L:                      # 每个线性层一份
        state      = alloc_zeros::<f32>(S_state)     # 零初始化：空历史
        conv_state = DeviceVec::zeros(S_conv)        # 零抽头
    seq_len = 0
```

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

模块文档一句话给出全部布局与 TP 结论，值得先读三遍：

- [src/recurrent_state.rs:L1-L9](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/recurrent_state.rs#L1-L9) — 声明每层状态为 `[local_value_heads, key_head_dim, value_head_dim]` f32、conv 状态为 `local_qkv_dim × (conv_kernel_dim - 1)` bf16，并预告 TP 下「每个 rank 拥有自己的状态、从不 all-reduce」。

两个结构体：

- [src/recurrent_state.rs:L20-L28](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/recurrent_state.rs#L20-L28) — `LayerRecurrentState`：`state: CudaSlice<f32>`（类型化 f32 切片）与 `conv_state: DeviceVec`（bf16 元素向量）。注释 `Stored as f32 per mamba_ssm_dtype="float32" in config` 引用的是上游 HF 配置的键名约定；注意本 crate 的 `RawConfig` 并**不**解析这个键（`TextConfig` 里没有它），f32 是无条件的选择，引用的是上游语义。
- [src/recurrent_state.rs:L30-L35](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/recurrent_state.rs#L30-L35) — `RecurrentState`：`layers: Vec<LayerRecurrentState>` 按**模型层序**存所有线性层（第 ℓ 个线性层对应 `layers[ℓ]`，与 `linear_idx` 计数器配套，见 4.3.3），`seq_len` 是 host 侧 token 计数。

布局公式的唯一权威来源：

### 4.2 causal conv1d：短记忆的入口与 prefill/decode 两条内核

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

在进入 GDN 递推之前，线性层先把融合投影出的 qkv 段过一遍**因果 depthwise conv1d**（再接 SiLU）。它是「短记忆」：只看最近 \(k_{conv}\) 个输入（当前 + 状态里的 \(k_{conv}-1\) 个抽头），输出写回给 GDN。卷积状态就是那 \(k_{conv}-1\) 个抽头，oldest-first 排列。

同一个语义有两套内核：

- **prefill**：一次处理整段（一个 chunk 的）token 序列，内核内部能直接看到历史 token，只需在结束时把**最后 \(k_{conv}-1\) 个输入**写进 conv_state，供下一段接续。
- **decode**：每个请求只有 1 个新 token，历史只能来自 conv_state；内核读抽头、算输出、**原地滚动**抽头，并与 SiLU 融合（输出是 `silu(bf16(conv))`，不是 `silu(sum)`， rounding 与参考实现逐位一致）。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

decode 一步（对槽 \(i\)、通道 \(c\)，卷积宽 \(k\)，抽头宽 \(w = k-1\)）：

\[
out_c = \mathrm{silu}\big(\mathrm{bf16}(\textstyle\sum_{j=0}^{k-1} w_{c,j} \cdot tap_{c,j})\big), \quad tap = [\,\underbrace{state_c[0..w]}_{\text{旧抽头}},\, x_c\,]
\]

随后状态滚动（oldest-first 移位，新输入顶到末位）：

\[
state_c[j] \leftarrow state_c[j+1]\ (j<w-1), \qquad state_c[w-1] \leftarrow x_c
\]

这正是 [src/recurrent.rs:L616-L647](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/recurrent.rs#L616-L647) 里参考实现 `reference_conv1d_decode_step` 逐行写成的内容——测试用它给 GPU 内核对拍。

**练习 1**：若 `linear_conv_kernel_dim = 1`，conv_state 多大？conv 还剩什么作用？

**答案**：GDN 块的输入约定就是「conv 后接 SiLU」，融合省一次内核发射与一次中间缓冲往返；而显式注明 rounding 顺序是为了与参考实现（以及上游 FLA）**逐位**一致——精度门（u8-l1）对这种舍入差是敏感的。

**练习 3**：prefill 内核明明能看到整段输入，为什么还需要 conv_state？
**答案**：prefill 是分块执行的（u4-l1）：第 N 个 chunk 的因果卷积需要第 N-1 个 chunk **末尾**的 \(k_{conv}-1\) 个输入，这正是上一个 chunk 结束时写进 conv_state 的内容。`conv1d_prefill_handoff_matches_single_prefill` 验证了这种接力与整段执行等价。

### 4.3 LinearStatePointerTables：为批量内核准备的每槽指针表

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

批解码一步要同时更新 N 个请求 × 24 个线性层的状态。若每个请求单独持有 `RecurrentState`，内核无法用一次发射索引到它们——CUDA 内核需要**设备侧连续的指针数组**。`LinearStatePointerTables` 就是这张表：每个线性层 ℓ 配一对 `CudaSlice<u64>`（`state_ptrs[ℓ]`、`conv_state_ptrs[ℓ]`），第 \(i\) 行是槽 \(i\) 的该层状态设备地址。

它成立的前提是一个不变量：**槽 \(i\) 的状态分配在请求生命周期内地址永不改变**。于是表可以一次建好、每个 decode token 反复重放——这正是 CUDA Graph 捕获需要的指针稳定性（图里烤进了这些地址，重放时读写同一位置）。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

一次批解码中线性层的执行序列（`padded_bs` 行，含 padding）：

```text
batch_decode_linear_attention_slots(attn, state_ptrs[ℓ], conv_state_ptrs[ℓ], padded_bs):
1. qkvz = GEMM(in_proj_qkvz, normed)          # [qkv+z, padded_bs]
2. ba   = GEMM(in_proj_ba,   normed)          # [2*Hv, padded_bs]
3. qkv_conv = conv1d_decode_batch(qkvz[:, :qkv_dim], conv_w, conv_state_ptrs[ℓ])
                                            # 内核按指针表原地滚动各槽 conv_state
4. o = gdr_decode_batch(qkv_conv, ba[:, :Hv], ba[:, Hv:], dt_bias, a_log, state_ptrs[ℓ])
                                            # 内核按指针表原地更新各槽 GDN state
5. g = rms_norm_gated(o, norm_w, z=qkvz[:, qkv_dim:])
6. attn_results = GEMM(out_proj, g); all_reduce_hidden(attn_results)   # TP 唯一通信点
```

表的两种构建方式：

- **固定行集**（单 GPU 图解码）：`from_recurrent_refs` 按精确 batch 建表填满，一次成型。
- **行集每步变化**（eager TP 解码）：`with_capacity` 按容量建一次空表，每步 `refill_from_recurrent_refs` 只把**活跃行** H2D 覆写进既有分配——零每步分配。

#### 4.3.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：为什么 `refill_from_recurrent_refs` 之后 batch 之外的行可以留着过期指针？
**答案**：内核拿到的 batch 计数参数就是活跃行数，GPU 线程按 `i < batch_size` 寻址，过期行根本不会被读；表按容量一次分配则是为了避免每步 cudaMalloc（既慢又破坏图/流语义）。

**练习 2**：`copy_state_to_slot` 与 `move_slot_within` 的调用时机分别是什么？
**答案**：`copy_state_to_slot` 在**请求 prefill 完成、加入 decode 批**时调用一次，把 prefill 瞬态状态灌进槽；`move_slot_within` 在 **TP 批内某请求中途退出**时调用，把最后一个占用槽搬进空出的槽，保证 decode 行密集（`0..bs`），这是 TP 图重放的行集前提（详见 u7-l3）。

**练习 3**：假如让每个请求的 `RecurrentState` 在 decode 中途重新分配（比如增长容量），会发生什么？
**答案**：设备地址改变，指针表过期，而已捕获的 CUDA Graph 里烤的还是旧地址——重放会读写已释放/错误的内存。所以本 crate 的所有状态操作（copy_from、move_slot_within）都是**向既有分配写入**，从不换缓冲。

### 4.4 TP 分片不变量：按 value head 分片、从不 all-reduce

#### 4.4.1 概念说明

GDN 状态天然按 value head 可分：状态是「每头一个 \([d_k, d_v]\) 矩阵」，头与头之间在递推中**互不交换数据**。于是 TP 的切法是：把 \(H_v\) 个 value head（连同 qkv 投影的对应行段、beta/alpha/dt_bias/a_log 等每头向量）均匀分给各 rank，每个 rank 只为自己那 \(H_v/W\) 个头维护并更新状态。分片是不相交的——各 rank 状态拼起来恰是完整状态，因此**没有任何理由对状态做 all-reduce**。

跨 rank 聚合只发生在回到 hidden 维的那一刻：`out_proj` 是行并行（各 rank 算出 hidden 维的**部分和**），随后一次 `all_reduce_hidden` 求和。这与 u2-l4 的结论「TP 通信点统一在回到 hidden 维处」一致，且模块文档直接写明状态「never all-reduced」。

#### 4.4.2 核心流程

TP 下每 rank 的状态尺寸：

\[
H_v^{local} = H_v / W, \qquad H_k^{local} = H_k / W
\]

\[
S_{state}^{local} = \frac{H_v}{W} \times d_k \times d_v, \qquad
S_{conv}^{local} = \Big(2 \frac{H_k}{W} d_k + \frac{H_v}{W} d_v\Big)(k_{conv}-1)
\]

分片正确性依赖两条上游约束：

1. **头分组不变量**（Config35 层）：\(H_v\) 是 \(H_k\) 的整数倍（一个 key head 服务一组 value head），`ConfigError::LinearHeadDivisibility` 强制。
2. **整除门**（LocalGeometry 层）：\(H_k\)（连同注意力头、KV 头、intermediate）必须被 \(W\) 整除，`TpIndivisible` fail-closed。

由 1、2 可推出 \(H_v\) 免检：设 \(H_v = m \cdot H_k\) 且 \(H_k = W \cdot k\)，则 \(H_v = W \cdot (m k)\)，自动整除——这就是 tp.rs 文档说「value-head count follows from the Config35 key/value-head invariant」的推理链。

每个 rank 状态字节占总量的比例：

\[
\frac{B_{req}^{local}}{B_{req}} = \frac{1}{W}
\]

（qkv 通道同样按行分片，conv 状态也随之精确减半。）**精确 \(1/W\)、零复制、零通信**。

#### 4.4.4 代码实践

**实践目标**：用数字验证「TP 下各 rank 状态精确减半、总和不变」，体会免检推理。

**操作步骤**（4B 配置，TP2）：

1. \(H_v^{local} = 32/2 = 16\)，\(H_k^{local} = 16/2 = 8\)。
2. state：\(16 \times 128 \times 128 = 262{,}144\) f32 = 1 MiB/层。
3. \(d_{qkv}^{local} = 2\times(8\times128) + 16\times128 = 4096\)；conv：\(4096\times3 = 12{,}288\) bf16 = 24 KiB/层。
4. 每请求每 rank：\(24 \times (1\,\text{MiB} + 24\,\text{KiB}) = 25{,}755{,}648\) B = 24.5625 MiB；两 rank 合计 \(= 49.125\) MiB，与 TP1 每请求总量**逐字节相等**。
5. 复核免检链：\(H_v = 32 = 2 \times H_k = 2 \times 16\)，\(H_k = 2 \times 8\) ⟹ \(H_v = 2 \times (2\times 8)\)，被 2 整除。再用 [src/config/tp.rs:L342-L359](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen35/src/config/tp.rs#L342-L359) 的测试 `requires_linear_attention_key_head_divisibility` 确认：只有 key head 不整除时才报 `TpIndivisible`。

#### 4.4.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：为什么 GDN 状态从不 all-reduce，而 MLP 的输出要 all-reduce？
**答案**：状态按 value head 不相交分片，各 rank 更新的切片拼起来就是完整状态，无信息重叠；而 `down_proj`/`out_proj` 是行并行，各 rank 只产出 hidden 维部分和，必须求和才能得到正确残差流。通信只发生在「回到 hidden 维」处。

**练习 2**：如果某配置 \(H_k = 17\)、\(H_v = 34\)、W=2，会触发哪个错误？
**答案**：`ConfigError::TpIndivisible { field: "linear_num_key_heads", value: 17, world_size: 2 }`。注意 \(H_v = 34\) 虽然能被 2 整除也救不了——免检的前提是 \(H_k\) 先过整除门，这正是 tp.rs 测试刻意保持 value = 2×key 不变量再只打破 key 整除性的原因。

**练习 3**：TP 下 f32 状态的精度策略变了吗？
**答案**：没有。状态仍是每 rank 本地的 f32 `[H,K,V]`，公式与内核与 TP1 完全相同（TP1 契约：W=1 时 local 即 global）；TP 改变的只是头数，而头数是内核的运行期参数。

## 6. 本讲小结

- `RecurrentState` = 24 份 `LayerRecurrentState` + `seq_len`；每层是 `[H_v^local·d_k·d_v]` 个 f32（GDN 递推状态，长期累积故用 f32）+ `[d_qkv^local·(k_conv-1)]` 个 bf16（卷积抽头，原样字节故用 bf16）。
- 所有尺寸出自唯一的 `per_layer_dims`；分配、显存预留、前缀快照槽数共享它，4B 每请求 49.125 MiB。
- causal conv1d 有 prefill（整段 + 末尾抽头落盘）与 decode（读抽头、原地滚动、融合 SiLU）两套内核，`conv1d_prefill_handoff` 证明 chunk 接力与整段等价。
- `LinearStatePointerTables` 用「槽地址终身不变」换来一次建表、token 间重放，是批量内核与 CUDA Graph 同时成立的前提；状态迁移原语一律向既有分配写入。
- TP 按 value head（连同 qkv 通道与每头向量）不相交分片，状态从不 all-reduce；唯一通信点是 `out_proj` 后的 `all_reduce_hidden`，各 rank 状态精确等于总量的 1/W。
- 头数是运行期参数、head dim 是编译期烘焙（128/128、卷积宽 ≤4）——config 加载期的三条门就是这两层事实的守门人。

## 7. 下一步学习建议

- **u3-l3（FFI 边界与内核封装）**：本讲只把 `gated_delta_rule_prefill_chunkwise_into` 当黑盒流水线；下一讲拆 `unsafe` FFI 调用的指针 guard 生命周期、`device_ptr`/`device_ptr_mut` 模式与 chunkwise 七段的算子契约。
- **u4-l1（Prefill 分块）**：本讲看到 conv/GDR 状态在单 chunk 内推进；下一讲看 `PREFILL_CHUNK_LEN` 如何把长提示切成 chunk 串行接力，以及 `GdrChunkwiseScratch35` 的保守预留。
- **u6-l1/l2（前缀缓存）**：`RecurrentStateStore` 的快照槽就是本讲的 `RecurrentState` 按预算复用——建议带着「快照 = 状态字节照搬」的直觉去读 `PrefixBoundaryKey` 与恢复路径。
- 想先摸执行全景的读者也可跳到 **u4-l2（batch_decode）**：本讲 4.3.2 的六步序列就是它核心循环的线性层分支。
